target_customer: Individuals and groups who want to track personal spending and shared expenses
problem: Tracking money across accounts and with friends was manual; users wanted easy transaction entry such as by email.
business_model: Freemium personal finance SaaS with paid tiers

founders.name: Shashank Pandit
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder; TechCrunch 2010 reports both founders took jobs at Facebook.

founders.name: Ashwin Bharambe
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in TechCrunch 2010 coverage; not on the YC page.

founders.name: Amit Manjhi
education: Carnegie Mellon University, PhD in Computer Science
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; previous startups listed there came after Buxfer.

competitors.name: Mint
competitors.traction_then: Passed one million unique visitors in the 2008 comparison; about 530K in the cited month

competitors.name: Wesabe
competitors.what: Personal finance community and bank data upload
competitors.traction_then: About 89,000 visitors in the cited 2008 month

competitors.name: Geezeo
competitors.what: Personal finance with mobile capabilities launched May 2007
competitors.traction_then: About 72,000 visitors in the cited 2008 month

technical_complexity.rationale: Transaction import, parsing and bank connectivity were standard but fiddly for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Well-funded Mint offered free automation and personal finance tools were easy to copy; Buxfer's email entry was a thin differentiator.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Intuit bought Mint; Buxfer stayed small, founders moved to Facebook by 2010.

market_need_then: Online personal finance traffic nearly tripled from 2007 to 2008 per Finovate, showing demand but dominated by free automatic tools.

identity.voice_and_tone: It's PERSONAL finance, user control and flexibility

branding.community_and_virality: Testimonials from users since 2007; press from TechCrunch, WSJ and Lifehacker per its site.

brand_strength.rationale: Press mentions exist but the name is easily confused with Buffer or Buxfer-like names and no brand-driven growth is documented.

outcome_analysis: Buxfer launched in the 2007 PFM boom against Mint, Wesabe and Geezeo with only about 315K raised from YC and an angel. TechCrunch reported in 2010 that both founders had joined Facebook and questioned who ran Buxfer. The product persists with a tiny team, so it stalled rather than shut down; the sources do not state a cause.
notes: CB Insights says Dead (latest round marked 2010-07-09) and 320K over 3 rounds; Seedtable and PitchBook say 315K. YC lists Active and the site is live, so exit none. Failure factors are inferred from the stall and founder departure, not stated by the company. Competitor traffic comes from a 2008 Finovate table, within about a year after the Winter 2007 batch. Founders: Bharambe from TechCrunch 2010, Manjhi from YC page; whether Manjhi was a founder at the start is not confirmed.
